reason: Narrower. In floras, 'higher order veins' means the tertiary and finer veins. PO's higher order leaf vein (PO_0008023) is fifth order and above only, so it is too narrow. This follows rule C270 (veinlet -> leaf lamina vein).
Narrower. A scape is a leafless peduncle arising from the base of the plant (rule C255). 'Inflorescence' only repeats what the word already says.

Broader name for an existing class. PO made 'laticifer' (PO:0005053) obsolete and points to the articulated and non-articulated laticifer cells instead. The flora does not say which kind, so the common parent, laticifer cell, is the safe target. Articulated laticifer (PO_0005006) applies only when the flora names it.
Narrower. These are bryophyte leaf-lobe cells measured in µm and described as hexagonal. 'Median' is a position word handled by the region context, like 'distal laminal cells'.

target: vascular leaf (PO_0009025), with the position 'lateral' in the leaf series (the lateral leaves of a dimorphic Selaginella shoot)
reason: Mistranslation of Spanish 'micrófilo lateral'. PO made microphyll (PO:0020053) obsolete, so lycophyte leaves are vascular leaves. Lateral versus median is a position in a series, which the patterns express.

target: petal (PO_0009032) part of flower (PO_0009046) with male (PATO_0000384)
reason: Failed to ground only because of the '(male)' qualifier. The sex inheres in the flower (flora_context_words), and the petal is part of that qualified whole.

target: higher order inflorescence axis (PO_0009081); 'secondary' -> second order inflorescence axis (PO_0006321), 'tertiary' -> third order inflorescence axis (PO_0006322)
reason: Narrower. Branches 20-28 cm long, with orders named, fit inflorescence branches (e.g. palm or panicle). PO lists 'secondary inflorescence branch' as a synonym of third order inflorescence axis (PO_0006322), which makes PO_0006321 a better fit for 'secondary'. 'Pinnate' leaves some chance of a bipinnate leaf rachis (pinna rachis FLOPO_0986065), so check the source.

target: trichome (PO_0000282) part of the rachis (inflorescence axis PO_0020122 or the leaf rachis, from context)
reason: Hair is a synonym of trichome. The hairs are part of a qualified whole, the rachis, which the patterns can express.
Narrower. The rays of an umbel or of a Euphorbia pseudumbel are inflorescence branches, and secondary rays are their branches. Do not confuse them with ray florets or wood rays.

target: seed (PO_0009010), surface region (side) of the seed; 'inner' face = adaxial side
reason: A face is a side or surface region of the seed. It is described as plane, concave, sulcate, smooth or polished, all of which the patterns express on the seed.

target: connective appendage (FLOPO_0986073), its ventral lobes (count/shape via lobed and the lobe-count pattern)
reason: The examples are 'apéndice del conectivo 2-lobado' (Melastomataceae). The lobes are divisions of the existing connective appendage class.
Narrower. The awns on Ericaceae-type anthers are dorsal appendages of the anther. PO's awn (PO_0025349) is limited to glumes, lemmas and paleas, so it does not apply.
Hairs of a named organ: trichome as part of the calyx.
Exact in sense. The collector (collecting) vein runs just inside the lamina margin (e.g. Myrtaceae), which is PO's intramarginal vein.

reason: Bare 'acumen' was rejected as a generic part. Here the organ is named: an acumen is the drawn-out tip of the corolla lobes.

target: plant organ base (FLOPO_0985024) part of corolla (PO_0009059)
reason: A base region of a named organ, which the patterns express.
The cupule class exists (FLOPO_0986036); the margin is a region of it.

The examples count rows of small, firm-walled cells, but they do not say which structure the rows belong to (leaf border, capsule mouth, etc.). A row is a way cells are arranged, not a part. Without the whole it cannot be grounded.

target: perianth (PO_0009058) part of flower (PO_0009046) with female (PATO_0000383)
reason: A part of a qualified whole; the sex inheres in the flower.
Narrower. A headlet is a small partial head, often one of the units of a compound capitulum (PO_0030122).
Narrower. These are bracts set among the flowers on a receptacle (e.g. peltate bracts in Moraceae). Flower bract has 'floral bract' and 'chaff' as synonyms.

Narrower or near-exact. In Amaranthaceae, the lobes of the filament tube between the stamens are the pseudostaminodes, which are recorded as present, triangular or linear. In other families an interstaminal lobe can be a lobe of the floral disc (FLOPO_0986094), so check the family.
Exact. This is Spanish 'labelo' mistranslated as 'label'. The qualities (sulcate, strongly arched, spotted, fleshy) describe an orchid lip.
Exact in sense. In succulent floras, 'leaf body' is the swollen leaf itself, given with three dimensions (length × width × thickness).
A fragment of a counting phrase ('spores 64 per sporangium'). The counted part is the spore (rule C259) within a sporangium (PO_0025094), as with 'per node' and 'per flower'.

target: peduncle (PO_0009053) part of inflorescence (PO_0009049) with female (PATO_0000383)
reason: Pistillate qualifies the inflorescence that the peduncle bears. It is a part of a qualified whole.
Failed to ground only because of the '(fruit)' qualifier. This is the fruiting-stage context ('sépales accrescents' in fruit), a stage context word in flora_context_words.

target: plant organ apex (FLOPO_0985023) part of stipule (PO_0020041)
reason: The appendage is the drawn-out, often subulate or spatulate, caducous tip of a stipule (e.g. Rubiaceae). Only one flora uses it, so it does not justify a new class. It can be expressed as the stipule apex, though that loses some meaning.

A mistranslation of Spanish 'caspilla', which is probably not 'capsule'. Something present or absent, brown, evanescent and caducous suggests a scurfy covering (indumentum, FLOPO_0986003), not an organ. Without the source this is too uncertain to ground.
A fragment of a relative measure ('1/4 de la longitud de la corola'). The bearer is the corolla, and length is the quality.
